bill.title: Establishes Social Media Research Center at four-year public institution of higher education.

posted_text:
🎓 NJ A4014 — NJ Wants to Study Social Media’s Impact on Kids

New Jersey is creating a Social Media Research Center at a state college to tackle growing concerns about social media’s effects on young people.

The state says it’s responding to warnings from the Surgeon General about potential harm – like increased rates of anxiety and depression among teens – linked to excessive social media use.

This new center will bring together experts to research how social media impacts kids’ mental and physical health, and develop recommendations for safer online experiences.

The center will also offer training modules to public schools and conduct research on age-appropriate screen times and content.

Importantly, state agencies like the Department of Health and Education will provide data to the center’s research, and the center will report back to the Governor and Legislature every five years on its findings.

Aug. 11, 2026: Approved P.L.2026, c.72.
